about: Fictional studies for the demo, of the same shape as a finished study: invented prose on illustrative figures. Laid beside the snapshot's own study.

studies.subject: MA
studies.question: Does MA still test as a Compounding Machine after the third quarter, and is the price above the base value?

sections.title: Core business
sections.guidance: What the company sells, to whom, how it is paid, and what it must do well to keep being paid. Name the segments and the share of revenue each brings.

sections.title: Growth
sections.guidance: Revenue, operating income, free cash flow and per-share figures over the last five years and the trailing twelve months, from the filings. Say what grew, what did not, and what drove it. Figures only from the facts given.

sections.title: Profitability and returns on capital
sections.guidance: Gross and operating margins, free cash flow margin and conversion, return on invested capital, and their direction. Separate the structural from the cyclical.

sections.title: Segments and unit economics
sections.guidance: Where the money is made and where it is lost, by segment or product, and what the marginal unit earns.

sections.title: Competition and position
sections.guidance: Who else does this, how the company wins or loses against them, and whether its share is rising or falling.

sections.title: Moats
sections.guidance: The sources of durable advantage (switching costs, network effects, cost position, intangibles, scale) with evidence for each, and how each could erode.

sections.title: Valuation
sections.guidance: Multiples against history and peers, what the price implies about growth and margins, and the gap to the owner's own valuation when one is recorded.

sections.title: Latest earnings
sections.guidance: What the latest quarter changed: the figures that moved, the guidance, and what management said it would do.

sections.title: Capital allocation
sections.guidance: Buybacks, dividends, acquisitions, debt and reinvestment: what the company did with its cash, at what prices, and whether it compounded value per share.

sections.title: Owner's valuation
sections.guidance: A discounted cash flow or equivalent in the owner's own terms: the drivers, the range, and what has to be true for each end of it. The owner records the base case; the study states the assumptions.

sections.title: Strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, threats
sections.guidance: Four short lists, each item tied to a figure or a fact above.

sections.title: Key research question
sections.guidance: The one question the thesis turns on, how it can be tested with data, and what the data says so far.

sections.title: Investment questions
sections.guidance: Why this business, why now, what the market misses, what would change the mind, and what is the downside if wrong.

sections.title: Classification
sections.guidance: Where the company sits in the methodology's classes, test by test, with the threshold, the figure and pass or fail. The app's checks below are the verdict; the prose explains them.
amendments: Class Macro Play: Asset class is etf. Diversified instrument expressing a multi-year macro view (E); tested first. Assumed here to be the ETFs held.

Class Transitional Holding: Asset class is equity; Revenue growth above 20; then at least 4 of 7: Return on invested capital at least 20; Gross margin at least 40; Operating leverage above 1; FCF conversion at least 1; Interest cover above 15; Revenue growth above 0; FCF per share growth above 0. Disruption engine (TTM revenue growth above 20%) and at least four of the seven A.2 thresholds; 20% cap.

Class Compounding Machine: Asset class is equity; Revenue growth at most 20; then at least 5 of 7: Return on invested capital at least 20; Gross margin at least 40; Operating leverage above 1; FCF conversion at least 1; Interest cover above 15; Revenue growth above 0; FCF per share growth above 0. At least five of the seven A.2 thresholds and no disruption engine; 10% cap.
Class Disruptive Growth Stock: Asset class is equity; then Revenue growth above 20. Disruption engine with fewer than four A.2 thresholds; 5% cap.

3.4: Sell on Quality Erosion: consistent drop in ROIC below 20% or sustained gross margin deterioration. (tested as for each symbol, average return on invested capital where asset class is equity at least 20.0%; watch)

sections.title: Kill signals and sell discipline
sections.guidance: The measurable conditions under which the position is sold or trimmed, from the methodology, and how far each is from tripping.
amendments: 3.1: During the accumulation phase each Compounding Machine is capped at 10% of total portfolio; excess from appreciation trimmed at the next quarterly review. (tested as for each symbol, total value to the owner where methodology class is compounding-machine, as a share of total value to the owner (of everything) at most 10.0%; hard limit)
E.6: Sell a Macro Play on thesis repricing, invalidation, exposure decay, structural failure or regime break. (yours to check)

2 Summary: Less than 71% and no disruption engine: no qualifying archetype; existing holding triggers 3.4 review within 30 days or Probation Hold. (tested as number of holdings where asset class is equity and no methodology class at most 0; watch)
D.4: Year-end vote on each Transitional Holding: graduate (trim to 10% within 30 days), maintain, or revert (trim to 5% within 30 days). (yours to check)

3.4: Sell on Quality Erosion: consistent drop in ROIC below 20% or sustained gross margin deterioration. (tested as for each symbol, average return on invested capital where asset class is equity at least 20.0%; watch)
3.4: Income-focused holdings: a dividend cut or suspension means immediate exit. (yours to check)
0: VIX > 30 signals extreme panic, historically associated with trough formation. (tested as max level of market indicators where indicator is VIX at most 30.00; watch)
0: VIX < 15 reflects complacency and low uncertainty. (tested as max level of market indicators where indicator is VIX at least 15.00; watch)
0: Monitor yield curve structure and inversion dynamics. (tested as max level of market indicators where indicator is US10Y2Y at least 0.00; watch)

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.guidance: What is good, what is acceptable, what is bad, and the action the methodology calls for. Not investment advice.

written.core-business: A fictional study for the demo. Mastercard Incorporated earns most of its revenue from value-added services and solutions and the lines around it; the segments and their shares are in the filings' revenue note.
written.growth: Revenue grew about 14.5% a year from 2021 to 2025, and 16.0% over the trailing year. Value-added services and solutions is the fastest line.
written.profitability: The operating margin is 58.3% and moved 2.6 points on the year; return on invested capital reads 98.0%.
written.segments: Value-added services and solutions grows faster than the company and carries a higher margin; the rest grows with the market.
written.competition: Competitors are named in the filing; share has held over five years on the figures the company reports.
written.moats: Scale and the network of customers on both sides are the advantages the study finds; each could erode if a rival matches the cost position.
written.valuation: At 32x trailing earnings and 33x free cash flow, the price assumes about 12.1% a year of growth on the reverse DCF.
written.earnings: The last four quarters beat the analysts' consensus on EPS; the guidance was kept at the last results.
written.capital-allocation: About 94% of free cash flow went back in buybacks and dividends.
written.dcf: On the base case the per-share value sits near the owner's base valuation; the bear case needs growth to halve.
written.kill-signals: Revenue growth below 8% is the kill signal on the record; it is not met on the latest figures.
written.classification: It tests as Transitional Holding on the filings' figures.
written.investment-questions: Whether the fastest line keeps its pace; whether the margin holds while the company invests; what the price assumes against that.
written.key-question: Does value-added services and solutions keep growing faster than the company for three more years? The study reads the figures as yes, with the guidance as the risk.
written.swot: Strengths: Value-added services and solutions, margins. Weaknesses: concentration in one line. Opportunities: new markets. Threats: regulation and rivals.
written.conclusion: A fictional conclusion: MA stays a Transitional Holding; the price is above the owner's base value.

written.segments: Family of Apps grows faster than the company and carries a higher margin; the rest grows with the market.
written.competition: Competitors are named in the filing; share has held over five years on the figures the company reports.
written.moats: Scale and the network of customers on both sides are the advantages the study finds; each could erode if a rival matches the cost position.
written.valuation: At 27x trailing earnings and 48x free cash flow, the price assumes about 24.9% a year of growth on the reverse DCF.
written.earnings: The last four quarters beat the analysts' consensus on EPS; the guidance was new at the last results.
written.capital-allocation: About 86% of free cash flow went back in buybacks and dividends.
written.dcf: On the base case the per-share value sits near the owner's base valuation; the bear case needs growth to halve.
written.kill-signals: Operating margin below 30% is the kill signal on the record; it is not met on the latest figures.
written.classification: It tests as Transitional Holding on the filings' figures.
written.investment-questions: Whether the fastest line keeps its pace; whether the margin holds while the company invests; what the price assumes against that.
written.key-question: Does family of apps keep growing faster than the company for three more years? The study reads the figures as yes, with the guidance as the risk.
written.swot: Strengths: Family of Apps, margins. Weaknesses: concentration in one line. Opportunities: new markets. Threats: regulation and rivals.
written.conclusion: A fictional conclusion: META stays a Transitional Holding; the price is above the owner's base value.
